Resolves #19547

The engine no longer keeps a second copy of every published release note. `.github/RELEASE_NOTES` now holds only the note being written (`v13.2.0.md`). The corpus already holds all 168 archived versions (v8.1.0–v13.1.0), chunked, in `neomjs/github-content-sync` `neo/release-notes`. Nothing kept the two copies equal, and they had drifted: at pin `1152671f7e`, 34 are byte-identical, 120 differ only in line endings and 14 in content, such as guide links the engine pinned to commits. The flat folder also grew toward GitHub's 1,000-entry listing cap.

`publish.mjs` keeps that shape: the release commit drops every note older than the version it releases, by version comparison alone. It never reads the corpus. A released note reaches the site through two separate steps: the content sync archives its GitHub Release, and Pages moves its corpus pin past it (pages README, step 1, before `update-neo-version`).

**Merge order:** neomjs/pages#23 first. It makes the site's step 4.1 read released notes from the corpus pin and add the tag's unreleased one, and it is backward-compatible with today's tags.

Evidence: L2 (unit specs over the publish lifecycle and the repository invariant, mutation-killed; the link guard; the Pages merge replayed on real data in #23) → L4 required for the deployed Portal listing every release (the 13.2 Pages build). Residual: AC-2's rendered Portal and AC-4's deploy, Residual-Owner: #14800.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `.github/RELEASE_NOTES` holds `v13.2.0.md` alone. `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` › *the engine holds no released note* asserts no note is older than `package.json`'s version. |
| AC-2 | The committed `releases.json` is regenerated from the engine (one leaf, `13.2.0`). The full list is the Pages build's: corpus 168 + engine 1 → 169 versions, no duplicate (replayed in neomjs/pages#23). The rendered Portal is Post-Merge. |
| AC-3 | `publish.mjs` still requires `v<version>.md` at its authored path and never removes it. `dropReleasedNotes(newVersion)` removes older notes in Step 2, before the index is rebuilt; the orphan spec pins both. The frontmatter contract now reads an archived note's shape from an inline fixture instead of the engine. |
| AC-4 | neomjs/pages#23 (the companion for neomjs/pages#22), merging first. |
| AC-5 | `git grep RELEASE_NOTES` audited. The remaining hits read the authored path (`publish.mjs`, `contentRoot.mjs`, `rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs`, the dev server, the workflow scope classifier) or describe history (the blogs' own text, ADR 0004's "authored flat in `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/`", still true). Links into the archive now point at GitHub Release pages: `ROADMAP.md`, `learn/blog/context-engineering-done-right.md`, and the two 13.2 blogs. The two 13.2 blogs would otherwise break at 13.3's publish. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The removal trigger, left open in the ticket, is the next release's own commit: at release N, every note older than N goes. It compares versions and reads no corpus, so the Engine-only release boundary holds. Delivering the dropped note to the site stays with the content sync and the Pages pin move. A cut whose Pages pin predates the sync would omit the previous note, which pages README step 1 already prevents.
- The 13.2 notes' split sentence now says the folder holds only the note being written. `CodebaseOverview.md` says the same.
- ADR 0004 is unchanged: it says the notes are *authored* in `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/`, which stays true.

## Test Evidence

- **Release unit specs:** 115/115 (`PublishReleaseNoteOrphan`, `ReleaseNoteFrontmatter`, `seo/Generate`, `RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo`, `WorkflowScopeClassifier`, `developmentThemeAssets`, `checkEngineBrainBoundary`).
- **Mutations:**
  - a stray `v13.0.0.md` turns the invariant arm red;
  - removing the `dropReleasedNotes(newVersion)` call turns the lifecycle arm red.
- **Link guard:** `check-relative-links`: 246 links resolved across 168 files.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The 13.2 Pages build (after neomjs/pages#23) lists v8.1.0–v13.2.0, and the Portal renders one archived note and the 13.2 note.
- [ ] At the 13.3 publish, the release commit drops `v13.2.0.md` and keeps `v13.3.0.md`.
